The opening of this passage is itself a rebuke of those so-called questioners and their questions. It is a matter for wonder that these people indulge in idle talk about something so plain and evident. The questions they raised were in fact about the Resurrection (qiyamah), and it was precisely this subject about which they were in great doubt and confusion, and over which they engaged in fierce dispute and debate. It did not occur to them that such a thing could come to pass, although it ought necessarily to be so, and the Resurrection is an entirely logical matter.

﴿عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ﴾ (78:1) "About what are they asking one another?" And about what they are conducting their debates, and then the answer itself is given. The meaning is that this question was not asked for the sake of seeking information; no knowledge was being sought. The question was posed merely to express wonder at their condition, and the implication is that the state of these people is worthy of astonishment, because their questions concern a matter of the greatest magnitude, about which they are in doubt, while its reality is thus.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 78, verses 2–3:

"About what are they asking one another? About the Great News, concerning which they are in disagreement." (78:2–3)

"Concerning the great news" is the phrase here: the great truth is not named explicitly; it is only called al-Naba' al-'Azim (the Great News), which is its attribute. This is done so that the tone of wonder and emphasis is sustained. Regarding that Day, the disagreements were between the believers and the disbelievers, between those who believed in it and those who denied it. The questions were in fact coming from those who denied it.

Then this question and idle talk is not answered, nor is it specified what the question and answer concern. Here only the greatness of that momentous matter is mentioned, and it is enough to give an allusive and indirect warning. This indirect warning is more effective than a direct answer, and it is more frightening.

Now, it appears outwardly that the direction of address has turned away from this great news to another subject, so that after a brief pause it may be taken up directly again. In fact, the direction of address turns toward certain realities, phenomena, scenes and signs present within this familiar universe of ours. If these are viewed with a seeing eye and reflected upon, they stir a tremor in human thought and reflection and are thought-provoking.

This journey is through the vast and wide expanse of this great universe. In this journey we see and observe countless scenes. These extensive scenes and countless imaginative images are presented to us through very limited and concise words. For this reason, when these scenes pass across the screen of the imagination within a very limited time and through limited words, they leave deep effects on thought and vision. It appears as though the plectrum of intellect and reason is striking the strings with great speed and continuity. All these ideas are presented in the style of an affirmative interrogation. It seems as though a powerful hand is awakening people who are sleeping in deep heedlessness, turning their hearts and vision toward observing this variety of God's creation. And it is calling them: reflect carefully on the governing power working behind this system, on how it has kept everything according to a measure. How this universe was created, and how it is being created. Can any intellect think that these creatures will be left as they are, with no reckoning and no accounting? Rather, there will be accounting, and when it occurs it will be a great news of the age, and its headline will be set. But alas, people hold differing opinions about this great reality. This journey has several stages; the first stage is the study of this earth.

﴿Have We not made the earth a bed?﴾ ... ﴿and the mountains as pegs?﴾ (78:6-7) “Is it not a fact that We made the earth a carpet, and drove the mountains in like pegs?” Mihad (bed, cradle) means prepared for travel and journeying, and also soft like a cradle. Both meanings derive from the word mihad and are close to each other. Whatever level of knowledge and understanding a person is at, and whatever stage of civilization and culture he is in, he understands this reality, that the earth is a cradle for him. To understand this as a fact, no great amount of knowledge is required. The firm fixing of mountains like pegs is also always visible to man, whether he is in the Stone Age or in the age of modern scientific progress. These realities are perceptible and can be discovered with ordinary attention.

However, the reality pointed to in these verses is somewhat deeper than the initial perceptions of Stone Age man. As man progressed in knowledge and understanding, he reached the depths of the realities of this universe. And these realities continued to shape human psychology. Man realized that behind this universe a profound wisdom and governance is at work, that a complex technology has been placed within it, that all creatures and existences are interconnected and mutually supportive, and that they are fulfilling one another's needs. And that this earth, especially, has been made a supportive and helpful cradle for human life. And that man is in harmony with this universe, and there is a kind of reconciliation between him and these cosmic forces.

The earth has been made a cradle for human life in a special way, and this is a proof whose truth cannot be doubted, provided the observer is not devoid of intellect and reason and is able to look behind this apparent universe. The truth is that the forces God has placed in this earth, if even a slight alteration is made in the composition of their ratios, or if the conditions of the earth were not what they are, or if one of the elements considered in the creation of the earth were removed and there occurred even the slightest disturbance in the ratios of this compound, then the earth which has been made a cradle for man would become a well of death for man, and the quality which the Qur'an is pointing to here would disappear from it. The Qur'an has only made a brief allusion here. It has left the details to man so that man may study the details according to his intellect, knowledge and experience.

And God drove the mountains into the earth like pegs. Every person, with a cursory glance, apparently finds that the mountains are fixed in the earth like pegs, in the same way as the pegs of a tent, and the mountains appear like tents. But what is their reality? From the Qur'an we find this, and we understand that they are extremely necessary for strengthening the earth, establishing its balance, and keeping it in place. It is also possible that these mountains were established so that a balance would be created on earth through the depths of the seas and the heights of the mountains, and it is also possible that through them a balance was established between the internal contraction and the surface contraction of the earth. And it is also possible that through these mountains, earthquakes and volcanoes were restrained at certain sensitive points of the earth, and that, apart from these reasons, the mountains were called pegs for some other unknown reasons which man has not yet come to know. Because the Qur'an made allusions to many unknown realities and clear indications, and mankind has discovered only a very limited part of them after centuries.

The Qur'anic verse: "And We created you in pairs" (78:8)

"And We created you in pairs" — ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾. This too is an extremely plain fact of this world, which a human being finds with great simplicity: that human beings have been created in the form of male and female. Then they were made into pairs, and through their union the chain of life has been kept going. Every person sees this reality and this scene, and then sees and feels how much delight, pleasure, joy and comfort has been placed within this system, and understanding these matters does not require any broad learning. For this reason Allah has placed this reality before human beings: the son of every civilization and culture also understands it, and every nomad and mountain dweller too perceives it through feeling, puts it into practice, and organizes life according to it.

Beyond this general awareness of this profound reality, there are some further matters worth reflecting upon, which are reached only by those who go somewhat deeper into knowledge and understanding, such as the making of the human germ and sperm into male and female, although within that germ there is no marker of male or female at all. It is Allah alone who leads one sperm towards maleness and another sperm towards femaleness. These are solely the works of the hand of divine power. Allah's creation and Allah's guidance place in whichever sperm He wills whatever characteristics He wills, so that human beings come into being in the form of a pair and the cart of life moves forward.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 78, verses 9–11:

﴿And We made your sleep a means of rest, and We made the night a covering, and We made the day a time for seeking livelihood﴾ (78:9–11). Consider the bounties of Allah: He created sleep for human beings so that they may gain rest and freshness. When sleep overtakes a person, it suspends for a time his faculty of perception and his faculty of action. During this interval, a person enters a state that can be called neither death nor life. By entering this state, all the fatigue of the human body and nerves is removed, and he rises refreshed and, as it were, newly created, and takes up the struggle and occupations of life again.

How sleep comes upon a person, and how as a result a person becomes refreshed, is a truth that only Allah knows; human will has no part in this matter, and a person does not know it. Nor does a person know how this freshness spreads into his body, because when he awakes he cannot imagine the state of sleep, and even during sleep his faculty of perception is inactive. This is an open secret concerning every living thing, known only to the Being who created these living creatures and made human life and its activities dependent upon sleep and rest. Every living creature can remain alive without sleep only for a limited time, and if it is forcibly kept awake artificially for a long period, it dies.

But there are also secrets in sleep beyond the bodily and nervous needs. It is also a means of tranquillity for the soul. It is a means of rest for the soul, drawing it away from the harsh struggle of life. Thus, just as a soldier removes his weapons and rests somewhat and enters a state of peace and tranquillity, yet in sleep he must go whether he wills it or not, because sleep is a need of human beings just as eating and drinking are needs. Sometimes sleep brings about a change that is no less than a miracle. A person suffers from spiritual exhaustion, his nerves are shattered, his soul is unsettled, and his heart is full of anxiety. Suddenly a drowsiness overtakes him, and sometimes this drowsiness lasts no more than a few moments. Yet freshness overtakes the body and soul of the individual, his condition undergoes a revolution, and within a few moments he feels himself refreshed, indeed like a new person. In the Battle of Badr and the Battle of Uhud, Allah sent down exactly such drowsiness upon the weary Muslims, which is called *nu'as* (drowsiness of security).

Allah says: ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him﴾ (8:11). And in Surah Al ʿImran: ﴿Then after the distress He sent down security upon a group of you, drowsiness overtaking them﴾ (3:154). And sometimes such conditions are also brought upon certain other people.

This *sabat* (cessation from the activities of life and of the intellect and soul) is a need of every living creature, and is one of the secrets of the Hand of Power and the Creator of the universe, and a blessing which is the pure outcome of Allah's bounty, gift and mercy. The Qur'an turns the human intellect and perception towards this: O human, reflect also upon your own distinctive properties, and contemplate a little upon the Hand of Power that has placed these properties in you, and seek to know Him.

Among the important powers and arrangements of the Divine Being is this: He has also harmonised the movement of this universe with the movement of creatures. Just as sleep has been placed within a human being to give him rest, so that after the struggle of life he may remain in some tranquillity, so within the universe Allah has created the environment of night, making a conducive atmosphere for human sleep and repose. Thus a harmonious environment has been created among Allah's creatures, and this entire world has become a family of living creatures. This family of living things responds to the demands of the properties placed within this universe, and within all the kinds of these living creatures have been placed movements and needs exactly as they are placed throughout this universe, and all these matters have been accomplished by the Hand of Power, thus producing complete harmony and accord between this universe and all of this living creation.

In these verses, a third aspect is also shown: the connection of the distant heavens and heights with the nearby earth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 78, verse 12:

{Qur'anic passage, 78:12–16:} "And We have built above you seven strong heavens, and placed therein a blazing and burning lamp, and sent down from the clouds abundant rain, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation and gardens of dense foliage."

The "mighty build" (shidad) that was raised above man refers to the seven heavens, and in another place they are called seven paths. What is the real intent behind them? Only Allah knows. It is possible that these seven are galactic systems. These galactic clusters are so vast that in one of them alone the number of stars is around one hundred million. And these seven clusters have a relationship with our earth and our solar system. The "mighty build" may also have another meaning, and no one knows this except Allah. Despite the great extent of our present knowledge about this universe, it is still very little.

What this verse tells us is that these seven heavens are extremely strong. Their structure is very firm, and they are so tightly joined together that no breakage or separation is possible at any point in them. These are the same heavens that we observe in this cosmic space, and upon which the word "heavens" is applied, and people understand it. The second point intended here is only to show that these seven strong heavens are also connected with the earth, and connected with human beings and all other living creatures. Therefore, these seven strong things are mentioned in the context of human life and the arrangements for its establishment and management.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 78, verse 13:

"And We have made a blazing lamp." And this blazing, hot lamp is the sun, whose light is intense and within which there is immense heat. Because of it the earth, and life upon it, becomes possible. It heats the waters of the seas and from them arranges the irrigation of this vast earth. It lifts up the clouds and carries them to the highest level of their height, and then the clouds are squeezed and rain is poured down.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 78, verses 14–16:

﴿And We sent down from the clouds water pouring forth abundantly﴾ (78:14). That is, by the laws of nature the water is wrung out of these clouds, and its water falls upon the earth. How this water is wrung out is a matter of how it occurs. It may be that water is squeezed from the clouds by the winds, and it may also be that water emerges through the process of lightning created by the clouds colliding with one another. But behind all these causes there is surely a Causer of causes, who is the Creator of all these causes and of the things that exert influence.

This sun has been called a lamp because within it there is a process of burning and light, and this very process is happening within the sun: there is a process of burning and a process of scattering light. Therefore the sun and the lamp are performing exactly the same function.

From the shining lamp of Allah there rains upon us warm rays and a downpour of light, and rain is continually wrung from the clouds. It falls repeatedly through the process of the crashing of lightning, and by this rain and this warmth every kind of vegetation comes into being on this earth, and from that vegetation come all the plants that human beings use, and all the dense gardens come into being. Al-Alfaf (translated as dense) refers to thick trees that are intertwined with one another, with the branch of one tree entwined in another.

This harmony in the creation of this universe is proof that behind it a wise hand is at work. Everything in it has been made with great wisdom and according to measure, and this same will is what sustains it, and every human being finds this truth if he directs his intellect and his consciousness toward it. But in the modern age, when humanity has progressed in knowledge and understanding, it has discovered what measures have been adopted in the creation of this universe, and how each and every thing in it has been made according to a formula. These formulas are so strange and astonishing that, on seeing them, the intellect begins to reel. And modern man, who possesses knowledge and understanding, and the scientist, regard it as absurd to think that this universe came into being merely by chance and accident; and those who flee from accepting a manager and creator of this universe are in truth afflicted with mere obstinacy and stubbornness. And their attitude is no longer viewed with respect.

The truth is that this universe has a Creator, and behind this universe a managing power is at work, which has created everything on a extremely sensitive scale, and all the forces of the universe are harmonious and interlinked with one another. And in this verse the Qur'an has pointed to this same order, harmony and divine design: that He made the earth a cradle, and made the mountains into pegs, and created people in pairs, made sleep a source of rest, made the night a means of covering and of repose for all, and arranged heat and light through the sun. And He arranged rains through the winds and the clouds, as a result of which vegetables, livestock and fruits are brought forth. All these realities, as they have been described, are also, from a scientific standpoint, mutually consistent and harmonious, and between them there is a profound connection of cause and effect. And it is this very connection that shows that this universe has a Creator who is arranging its system with extraordinary beauty and wisdom, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Powerful. If these scientific and observable realities are read with open eyes, a person receives from them a very great message of wisdom and understanding, and after that he receives a great message, whose headline is that a Day of Decision is coming.

﴿All these creatures are here for your benefit; eat and drink and enjoy yourselves, but there is also a day that is coming; it is the Day of Decision, the Day of Judgment.﴾

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 78, verses 14–16:

﴿And We sent down from the clouds water pouring forth abundantly﴾ (78:14). That is, by the laws of nature the water is wrung out of these clouds, and its water falls upon the earth. How this water is wrung out is a matter of how it occurs. It may be that water is squeezed from the clouds by the winds, and it may also be that water emerges through the process of lightning created by the clouds colliding with one another. But behind all these causes there is surely a Causer of causes, who is the Creator of all these causes and of the things that exert influence.

This sun has been called a lamp because within it there is a process of burning and light, and this very process is happening within the sun: there is a process of burning and a process of scattering light. Therefore the sun and the lamp are performing exactly the same function.

From the shining lamp of Allah there rains upon us warm rays and a downpour of light, and rain is continually wrung from the clouds. It falls repeatedly through the process of the crashing of lightning, and by this rain and this warmth every kind of vegetation comes into being on this earth, and from that vegetation come all the plants that human beings use, and all the dense gardens come into being. Al-Alfaf (translated as dense) refers to thick trees that are intertwined with one another, with the branch of one tree entwined in another.

This harmony in the creation of this universe is proof that behind it a wise hand is at work. Everything in it has been made with great wisdom and according to measure, and this same will is what sustains it, and every human being finds this truth if he directs his intellect and his consciousness toward it. But in the modern age, when humanity has progressed in knowledge and understanding, it has discovered what measures have been adopted in the creation of this universe, and how each and every thing in it has been made according to a formula. These formulas are so strange and astonishing that, on seeing them, the intellect begins to reel. And modern man, who possesses knowledge and understanding, and the scientist, regard it as absurd to think that this universe came into being merely by chance and accident; and those who flee from accepting a manager and creator of this universe are in truth afflicted with mere obstinacy and stubbornness. And their attitude is no longer viewed with respect.

The truth is that this universe has a Creator, and behind this universe a managing power is at work, which has created everything on a extremely sensitive scale, and all the forces of the universe are harmonious and interlinked with one another. And in this verse the Qur'an has pointed to this same order, harmony and divine design: that He made the earth a cradle, and made the mountains into pegs, and created people in pairs, made sleep a source of rest, made the night a means of covering and of repose for all, and arranged heat and light through the sun. And He arranged rains through the winds and the clouds, as a result of which vegetables, livestock and fruits are brought forth. All these realities, as they have been described, are also, from a scientific standpoint, mutually consistent and harmonious, and between them there is a profound connection of cause and effect. And it is this very connection that shows that this universe has a Creator who is arranging its system with extraordinary beauty and wisdom, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Powerful. If these scientific and observable realities are read with open eyes, a person receives from them a very great message of wisdom and understanding, and after that he receives a great message, whose headline is that a Day of Decision is coming.

﴿All these creatures are here for your benefit; eat and drink and enjoy yourselves, but there is also a day that is coming; it is the Day of Decision, the Day of Judgment.﴾

People were not created in vain, nor are they left aimlessly unaccountable. The arrangements of their lives, which were mentioned in the preceding verses, and the order of the universe in which they live are fully in harmony with each other. After careful reflection, every wise person reaches the conclusion that human beings are not purposeless and irresponsible, free to do good or evil on earth and then turn to dust after death, with no one to question them whether they were on the path of guidance or the path of misguidance, whether they acted justly or unjustly on earth.

Nevertheless, there is certainly a Day of Judgment, on which all the matters of the past will be decided. This is a fixed and appointed day, whose rites and rules are settled, and whose time is also fixed and determined with Allah. ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time﴾ (17:78). On that day the system of this universe will change, and the bonds of this system will be loosed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 78, verse 18:

"On the Day when the Trumpet is blown, you will come forth in throngs, and the heaven will be opened and will become gateways, and the mountains will be set in motion until they become a mirage."

The Trumpet (ṣūr) means the horn. We know only its name and know that it will be blown into. As to how it will be, we should not delve into that. Even if we were to learn its detailed nature, it would make no difference to our faith. Allah has protected our power of understanding from being consumed by such fruitless topics, and He has told us as much knowledge as was needed. Therefore we think only this: there will be a sound, and as a result all human beings will rise up from their graves. The image that comes to our minds is of human generations coming on in throngs. However, in the world Allah had established a system whereby earlier generations passed away and new generations took their place, so that the earth would not run out of room for people to live. Nevertheless, these verses tell us that people will come in throngs from every high and low place. They will be in one single field. They will emerge from their graves like ants, and they will be so numerous that neither their first row nor their last will be known. This great gathering will be producing fear in hearts, because no one has ever seen or imagined such a great gathering, since this gathering will take place on the Day of Resurrection. Where it will take place we have no knowledge, because this system of the universe will be destroyed. Great calamities and upheavals will already have occurred.

"And the sky will be opened, until it becomes gateways, and the mountains will be set in motion until they become a mirage." (78:19–20)

This mighty sky will be opened, and it will become gateways, meaning it will split apart and cracks will appear in it, as has been mentioned in other surahs. This is a situation of which we cannot fully form an idea. The great mountains will move and become a mirage. That is, if the mountains themselves are reduced to fine particles and scattered in the air, and they will appear just as a mirage does. As has been mentioned in other surahs, just as a mirage has no real existence, so too the mountains will vanish and become dust, and these particles will reflect light in the manner that light is reflected in a mirage, where water appears. In short, terrifying changes will take place in this universe, and this upheaval will come after the blowing of the Trumpet. This is the Day of Decision; it is decreed, and by the wisdom and planning of Allah all these events will occur.

Now, a glimpse of the judgment of the righteous and the wicked, some events that come a little later than the events occurring immediately after the blowing of the Trumpet. But first the judgment of those who are wicked is announced.

﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or any drink, except scalding water and dark, foul liquid.﴾ (78:24)

"They will not taste in it any coolness or anything fit to drink." Yet they will certainly be given something to drink. What will it be? Very bitter and loathsome.

Verse 78:25: "Nothing will they get except boiling water and the pus-discharge of wounds." Scalding water that will scorch their throats and stomachs. This is their "coolness" (the term is used ironically), and ghassaq is the fluid that flows from the wounds of those who have been burned; this is their drink.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 78, verse 26:

﴿جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا﴾ "A full and fitting recompense." They shall be repaid in full for what they earned and for what they sent ahead, stored up for the Day of Resurrection.

The passage quotes verse 78:27 with its opening words elided ("انھم ..."), so I translate the text exactly as it stands.

"They did not expect any reckoning" (78:27). And they did not believe in the occurrence of the outcome of good and evil deeds.

"And they utterly denied Our signs," (78:28). The rhythm of these words shows that they were intense in their denial and persistent in rejecting it. Yet Allah was recording their deeds, and this record was so complete and comprehensive that no matter, great or small, could escape it.

The passage contains a Qur'anic quotation with the verse reference given as (29:78), which appears to be a citation error: the verse quoted, "وكل شيء أحصيناه كتابا" (An-Naba 78:29), is from Surah 78. I translate the text as it stands.

And [the Qur'an states]: ﴿And We had recorded everything in a book, enumerated.﴾ (29:78)

Now they are being severely reproached here.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on surah 78, verse 30:

﴿Now taste [it]. We will increase you in nothing except punishment.﴾ (30:78)

Now the scene of the opposite party appears. This is the scene of the people of piety and of the blessings in which they live in comfort. After the rebels and the disobedient, it was also necessary to show a glimpse of them.

In the first scene, Hell was prepared and laid out as a dwelling for the disbelievers, and it lay in wait for them the way a hunter lies in ambush, seizing them one by one. In the same way, no one could escape from Hell. In this scene, it appears that the people of Paradise have attained the station of salvation and success. And this place is the place of salvation and success.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 78, verses 32–33:

"Gardens and grapevines" (78:32): in the form of "gardens and grapes." The grapevine is singled out specifically because the addressees of the Holy Qur'an were well acquainted with it. "Kawā'ib" means young, tender, maidens whose breasts are round; and "atrāb" means equal in beauty and charm, and of the same age in terms of the root "sanah" (year).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 78, verse 34:

﴿And a overflowing cup.﴾ That is, full to the brim.

The outward form of these blessings is sensory, and they are mentioned by naming things so that the meaning comes close to people's understanding. As for their reality, it is not possible for the people of the earth to grasp it, because their comprehension is confined within earthly concepts. Their general and spiritual conditions will be in accordance with Islamic taste and conscience. A Muslim is aware of them in that

Surah 78, verse 35: "They will hear therein no idle talk or lying."

That is, they will be living in a state where there will be no idle talk in it. And there will be no lying in it, because lying usually leads to the beginning of strife and disputation. There, the realities will be open and no one will have the opportunity for argument and debate. Nor will there be any talk there that is without benefit and contains no good. This state of affairs is fitting for that world which is the abode of eternity.

Verse 78:32–38 ("Recompense ... an account") — the Qur'anic quotation is already in the text, so I begin with the commentary.

Recompense... and abundant reward from your Lord. Here the grace of the mode of expression, the melodious sound, and the distribution of recompense and bounty are worth observing. The intensity of the rhymes (fawasil) and the rhyming endings (qawafi), and their phonetic harmony, are a distinctive feature throughout this whole section (juz') and are very beautiful.

The scenes of that Day, about which those who ask questions ask, and about which those who differ dispute, now come to an end. At its conclusion, observe a scene beautiful in both wording and meaning, in which Jibril (ʿalayhi al-salam) and the other angels stand in ranks. They all stand before the Most Merciful (al-Rahman), and none of them can speak except one who has been given permission. It is a awe-inspiring and frightening station.

This retribution and punishment, which was described in detail earlier for the people of taqwa (God-consciousness) and for the people of misguidance, comes from your Lord. And

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful﴾ (78:37)

(from the Most Merciful God, who is the owner of the earth, the heavens, and everything between them). This is now the appropriate moment for this final touch and the declaration of this great truth: that the lordship (rububiyyah) of Allah encompasses the heavens and the earth, and within it are both this world and the Hereafter. It gives reward to the people of taqwa, gives punishment to the people of misguidance and transgressors, and all decisions of this world and the Hereafter return to Allah. Furthermore, this lordship is most merciful. This reward is also the result of His mercy, and the punishment is also the demand of His mercy. It is from the demand of His mercy that rebellious ones are burned in Hell, because it is a pure mercy that evil be punished, and that good and evil not be treated equally; otherwise that would be injustice.

Then this mercy carries majesty within it. On that dreadful day, no one will be able to speak in this court of mercy. Even Jibril (peace be upon him) and the other exalted angels will stand silently in rows. Only with permission may one present something, and then speech will take place. But even that speech will be correct, for the Most Merciful knows what is in the heart, and there will be no permission at all to say something evil.

This scene, in which innocent people and leading angels stand silently in that presence, with no one even speaking, spreads over the atmosphere clouds of awe, dread, majesty and dignity. In such circumstances, when clouds of fear hang overhead, those heedless of the world and those rushing headlong on wrong paths are once again warned, and a mighty cry comes, and an attempt is made to awaken those who are intoxicated.

This is a severe jolt. Those who doubted this true Day and raised skeptical questions about it are being shaken with the utmost force.

﴿That Day is the Truth﴾ (39:78). Therefore there is no room for skeptical questions about it. O people! The times of leisure are still available; you have respite. Make use of it.

﴿Whoever wills may take a path to his Lord, a return﴾ (39:78). Before Hell lies in ambush and seizes you in its grip.

This is a stern warning. Even one who is in deep slumber can awaken.

﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾ (40:78) "We have warned you of a punishment that has drawn near." It is not far off. This is the punishment of Hell, which awaits you, as you have seen in this scene. This worldly life is but a brief journey, and the boat of your life is about to reach the shore.

This punishment will be so severe that the disbeliever will loathe his very existence and will wish that he had been made non-existent.

﴿On the Day when a man will look upon what his hands have sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾ (40:78) "On the day when a person sees all that his hands have sent forward, and the disbeliever cries out, 'Would that I were dust!'" This is the utterance of one who is extremely constricted in heart and despairing.

Now fear and remorse cover the atmosphere, for the living human being wishes to become non-existent and turn into dust and dirt. Only through his non-existence can he save himself from this terrifying punishment. This will be the stance of those who today raise doubtful questions about this great reality and this reality that makes headlines, and who put forward suspicions.
